Listen to this article Share The Owu descendants in Oyo State, comprising over 200 family compounds across Ibadanland, Owu Oyo, Ogbomoso, Oke-Ogun and Ibarapa, have unanimously declared support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reelection as well as endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) Oyo State Governorship Candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, and his running mate, Adesoji Adedeji, as their preferred candidates for the forthcoming 2027 gubernatorial election. Advertisement Advertisement The endorsement was announced at the Omo Olowu Conference held at the International Conference Centre, Ibadan in which Mogajis, traditional Baales, family heads, prominent stakeholders and sons and daughters of Owu ancestry from different parts of Oyo State were in attendance. The conference was hosted by Teslim Olugbode, Mogaji Olugbode of Ibadanland, while Subair Olajuwon, Mogaji Ile Nla, delivered the welcome address, setting the tone for the gathering and emphasising the importance of unity, collective responsibility and the preservation of Owu heritage. The Conference, which marked a significant milestone in the collective engagement of Owu descendants, provided a platform for cultural preservation, heritage development, unity and discussions on the political direction of the Owu people ahead of the 2027 general elections. The gathering was graced by the Royal Father of the Day, the Olowu of Kuta, Oba Hameed Adekunle Oyelude Makama, who called on Owu descendants and stakeholders to support the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, ahead of the 2027 presidential election. In his remarks, Oba Olowu Kuta appreciated the impressive turnout of Owu family representatives and encouraged them to sustain the spirit of unity, solidarity and collective responsibility in advancing the interests of the Owu-Anlugbua lineage. Advertisement Speaking at the Conference, Sharafadeen Alli expressed profound appreciation to the Olowu lineage stakeholders, Mogajis, traditional Baales and members of the Owu family for their support and confidence in his political aspiration. He assured the gathering of his commitment to supporting Owu heritage and promoting the interests of the Owu people if given the opportunity to serve as Governor of Oyo State, by God’s grace. He also acknowledged the importance of traditional institutions and indigenous family structures in promoting peace, cultural preservation and community development. Advertisement The keynote speaker, Olusola Adebayo Akinsowon, delivered an insightful lecture on the theme, “The Role of Owu People in Nation Building.” His presentation examined the historical contributions of the Owu people, their cultural heritage and the need for greater unity, participation and collective responsibility in shaping the future of society. The conference witnessed the participation of over 200 Owu family compounds, represented by their respective Mogajis and traditional Baales, reinforcing the collective commitment towards a united Owu identity across Oyo State. Advertisement Advertisement The Omo Olowu Conference was conceived as a strategic platform to strengthen relationships among Owu descendants, promote the preservation of ancestral heritage and establish a common voice for the Owu-Anlugbua lineage in the socio-cultural, economic and political development of Oyo State. The successful hosting of the conference represents another step towards consolidating the unity achieved through previous engagements with the Olowu of Kuta and other traditional stakeholders. The organisers expressed appreciation to the Royal Father of the Day, political leaders, keynote speaker, Mogajis, traditional Baales, family representatives and all participants for their contributions towards the success of the historic gathering. They reaffirmed their commitment to sustaining the Omo Olowu platform as a vehicle for cultural preservation, peaceful coexistence, traditional development and constructive engagement in the affairs of Oyo State and Nigeria. Meanwhile, the founder of Ilaji Resort and Businessman Jubril Dotun Sanusi, has been honoured with the prestigious Distinguished Service Award by the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Oyo State Council, in recognition of his selfless service and invaluable contributions to society. The award was presented to Sanusi by the Chairman of the NUJ Oyo State Council, Akeem Abas, during activities marking the Union’s 60th Anniversary Diamond Jubilee (1966–2026). The distinguished recognition celebrates Sanusi’s unwavering commitment to humanitarian service, community development and societal advancement, which have continued to earn him commendation and recognition across various sectors. In his response, Okanlomo Oodua and Gbonka Olubadan of Ibadanland, Sanusi expressed profound appreciation to the leadership and entire members of the NUJ Oyo State Council for finding him worthy of the prestigious honour. He described the recognition as a source of encouragement to deepen his commitment to service to humanity and contribute more meaningfully to the development of society. The award further highlights the importance of collaboration between the media, community stakeholders and individuals whose contributions continue to promote social development and the collective good. The JDS Support Group congratulated Jubril Dotun Sanusi on this well-deserved recognition, describing the honour as another testament to his dedication to humanity and his enduring commitment to making positive contributions to society. The Group also felicitated the Nigeria Union of Journalists, Oyo State Council, on its 60th Anniversary Diamond Jubilee, commending the Union for six decades of dedication to professional journalism, responsible media practice and societal development.
